edit.description: the verb's read of the target directory's lockfiles, and what it says when the installer reads none of them
the init cases over a repo with and without a lockfile the installer reads
the `setup` clause's account of what adoption owes a repo the installer cannot read

summary: `flume-harness init` over a repo whose lockfiles the shipped installer does not read names `setup` as what the declaration owes, instead of writing a chain whose first load refuses
acceptance: init over a directory holding no lockfile the engine's installer reads says so and names `setup` as what the consumer must declare before a tick can run; init over a directory it does read writes the same skeleton it writes today
tests: init over a repo with no lockfile the installer reads names `setup` as what the declaration owes
pins: init over a repo holding a lockfile the installer reads writes its skeleton unchanged
notes: The undeclared-`setup` arm refuses at chain load (`harness/provisioning.ts`) for a tree with no lockfile the installer names, and `installPlan` (`src/setupWorktree.ts`) already reports the whole set it reads — so the probe is a read, not a second rule. A commented row does not load; the skeleton cannot guess a yarn or bun install, which is why the loud door is at adoption rather than a default.
